Islam and Judaism are not strangers but siblings. They share roots, rituals, and a long history of coexistence. Remembering this “Judeo-Islamic tradition” isn’t nostalgia; it’s a blueprint for pluralism and peace in a fractured age, explains Cato’s @AkyolinEnglish.
ow.ly/b6i650YBsI7

President Trump’s tariffs on some imported on-patent drugs will make US citizens poorer and critical medicines more expensive and scarce, explains Cato’s @mfcannon. 

ow.ly/mlyl50YCZjA

The White House has requested a $1.5 trillion defense budget for 2027—a historic high. If the military already “has everything it needs,” why spend another $500 billion, ask @JustinTLogan and @GiltnerBen. Strategy should drive the budget, not endless expansion.

The Logos Tutoring Program separates middle school boys from civilization twice a week for three years—on 50 acres in rural Georgia. They learn ancient Greek, permaculture, and how to face failure. Cato's @ColleenHroncich profiles the result. 

ow.ly/YZlq50YCm0L

Trump’s “reciprocal” tariffs were explicitly imposed to reduce the US trade deficit, but it reached an all-time high (in real terms) in 2025. Check out the new analysis from Cato Institute scholars. 

ow.ly/OxWi50YCvKw

Britain’s new steel plan mimics an ongoing fallacy America has adopted—using national security to justify broad protectionism. This won’t make the UK safer, it will make steel‑dependent industries poorer and the economy less productive, says Cato’s @MrRBourne.

ow.ly/vKan50YCz8g

Ex-US Attorney General Pam Bondi tried to turn the DOJ into a political weapon aimed at enemies of President Trump, but the cases fell apart in court. No "wins," just damage to the rule of law. In the end, even Trump lost patience. Loyalty isn’t justice, says Cato’s @foxmike90.

ow.ly/gvQp50YCVox

President Trump’s tariff regime sparked a lobbying surge that reached levels not seen in years, if not decades, Cato scholars report: 

🔹 +218% more tariff-related clients in 2025 
🔹 $900M+ spent in the first half of 2025 alone 

Learn more from Cato’s @scottlincicome, @AlfredCObregon, and Chad Smitson:
ow.ly/FfNC50YCvjb

Viktor Orbán has concentrated power, dismantled liberal democracy, and undermined the rule of law and freedom of the press, says @johanknorberg. The result is a less free Hungary. 
  
Explore Norberg’s latest research on how Orbán’s Hungary eroded the rule of law and free markets. 
ow.ly/pyf650YBSel

Federal debt is already near 100% of GDP — and rising faster than economic growth. 

The longer Congress waits, the harder the fix. 

According to Cato’s @RominaBoccia, closing the gap today requires adjustments equal to 4.7% of GDP. Wait until 2046? That jumps to 6.9%. 

ow.ly/HPc350YAOYT

President Trump treats America like his personal empire—waging unnecessary wars, enriching allies and himself, ignoring Congress, and leaving civilians and global stability in ruins, says Cato’s @Doug_Bandow. This is not what the Founders envisioned.
ow.ly/3jyz50YClmN

The US deficit isn’t a revenue problem—it’s a spending problem. Taxes on the wealthy or new levies won’t fix deficits: high taxes shrink the base, and 98% of revenue shortfalls come from unchecked government spending, says Cato’s @veroderugy.
ow.ly/GNjU50YC3MG

The government has illegally collected more than $160 billion in IEEPA tariffs. Now, US taxpayers are on the hook for about $700 million in additional interest payments for every month that refunds are delayed, according to Cato Institute scholars. 

ow.ly/fu5050YCwb8

Cato’s @foxmike90 warns of a growing “remedy-free zone,” where legal doctrines shield federal agents from accountability. State statutory remedies are a way to push back, but Fox warns that a guaranteed and consistent accountability mechanism ultimately requires congressional action.
ow.ly/molf50YClzY

Can the government permanently strip someone of their Second Amendment rights for a past felony? 

Cato joined an amicus brief with the ACLU of North Carolina Legal Foundation, arguing that North Carolina’s blanket firearm ban for all felons—regardless of violence, history, or time since conviction—is unconstitutional. 
ow.ly/zUEM50YBSlW

The data confirm that—contrary to White House promises—there was no tariff-related hiring boom in 2025, Cato scholars report. 

ow.ly/yIb350YCvHK

TSA agents staying home, hours-long airport lines, and Congress still cannot agree on a DHS funding bill. Cato’s Pat Eddington and @CatoEdwards say this is a consequence of tying aviation security to the federal budget, a mistake other high-income countries do not make.
 
Listen to the new Cato Podcast episode!
 
Apple: ow.ly/txu850YCoAA
Spotify: ow.ly/74RA50YCoAB
Our website: ow.ly/BbYA50YCoAz

Despite the president’s “Liberation Day” prediction of a boom in foreign direct investment, quarterly FDI has fallen since April 2025, Cato scholars report. 

Total FDI in 2025 was $288.4B, lower than the annual totals from 2021 through 2024, and far short of the rate needed to reach the president’s goal of $18T in investment.
